Inventory: one whole-order clause with two operative sentences (an incumbent without competitive status acquires it upon an agency head's recommendation made within one year from the date of the order if four conditions are met, and the Civil Service Commission is to promulgate regulations). Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table row for 10080 describes it as authorizing certain Government employees to acquire a competitive civil service status. The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The one-year period for agency recommendations ended on 1950-09-30 on the inclusive reading (the exclusive reading, under which the period ends when that day begins, would end it on 1950-09-29); it limits new recommendations but not acquisition by a person already recommended, who must still pass a noncompetitive examination, and the order stayed on the books until express revocation. The sunset is therefore disclosed as a partial own-terms limit and not claimed as the first end of the clause. Later orders that recite 10080 are not ends: Executive Order 10103 (1950-02-01) deems certain employees of international organizations to have been in active-duty status on 1949-09-30 so far as 10080 is concerned, and Executive Order 10535 (1954-06-09) lets the Civil Service Commission confer competitive status on persons who met the requirements of 10080 or of Executive Order 10157 but were not recommended because of administrative error; neither amends 10080's text, extends its one-year period or revokes it.
